about: CHAIN york_954 (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/york_954.md; words Data/writing/chain_york_954.json). York between the kings of Dublin, Eric son of Harald and the king of the English, 947 to 954: the richest market in the north and the hardest to keep a friend in. Fourteen cards: ten steps (s01 to s10, one of them a crew card) and four endings. Step flags ch_york_954_1 .. _10; leanings ch_york_954_lean_hall, _lean_dublin, _lean_town; what the player did: _hosted, _paid, _slipped, _tally, _dublin_cargo, _dublin_friend, _captives, _ransomed, _erics_peace, _wulfstan_letter, _kings_ear, _informer, _oswulf_man, _knows_plot, _sent_word, _called_dublin, _stood_town, _eric_aboard, _tried. Endings: ch_york_954_end_stainmore (what happened), ch_york_954_end_town (what happened, the honest road), ch_york_954_end_eric_lives (history changed: changed_stainmore_eric_lives), ch_york_954_end_dublin (history changed: changed_york_dublin_kingdom_954). Lasting costs: ch_york_954_blood_money, ch_york_954_oswulf_feud, ch_york_954_eadreds_enemy. Every drawn step is also scheduled by the step before it where the day is known, so no step is lost. Each option's note names its outcome text. The Chronicle is quoted from Ingram 1823. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite. (?) marks what could not be checked.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Eoforwic, 947 to 951). A new penny with every king: the moneyer will not take last season's coin at its face. Sources: the York coinage of 939-954 (Blunt, Stewart and Lyon 1989; Blackburn 2004; realms/northumbria_york.json coins): Olaf's raven, the three-cornered knot and the banner, ERIC REX with a sword; the moneyer Ingelgar struck for Olaf Sihtricson and for Eric, and is known from his coins alone. Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D 947, 948, E 949 for who is king. That a stranger traded through a host is the realm file's reading (?). Cast: Ingelgar (real, the name on the coins); the host Ulfketil is invented (Ulf- + -ketil, the English Ulfcytel). Sets ch_york_954_1; _hosted.

cards.note: Step 2 (scheduled ten days after step 1; also drawn). The host shows the three doors a stranger can knock at: the king's hall, the minster, the Dublin men on the landing. Sources: Archbishop Wulfstan I (931-956) leads the Northumbrian council (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D 947); York and Dublin under one kindred from 919 (realms/northumbria_york.md); the Coppergate finds for what the town makes and buys: combs, jet, amber, silk (Hall 1984; dossiers/eoforwic.md). The steward and the Dublin shipmaster are invented: Arnketil (Arn- + -ketil), Gilli (a Norse-Gaelic byname, attested later (?)). The riddle is Exeter 20 (riddles_793.json). Sets ch_york_954_2 and one leaning.

cards.note: Step 3 (scheduled thirty days after step 2; drawn from 948). King Eadred has harried the land and burned Wilfrid's minster at Ripon; the Northumbrians give up Eric and pay for the wrong. Source: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D 948 (Ingram 1823: 'they then abandoned Eric, and compromised the deed with King Edred'). How the payment was raised is not recorded: the game has it gathered on the landing, from strangers too, and still being gathered in later years (?). The clerk is invented, unnamed. Sets ch_york_954_3; _paid, _slipped or _tally.

cards.note: Step 4, a turn (scheduled after step 3; drawn 949 to 951; a player who comes late skips it). Olaf Sihtricson, called Cuaran, is king at York again. Source: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle E 949 (Ingram 1823: 'This year came Anlaf Curran to the land of the Northumbrians'). What York sends to Dublin and Dublin wants: combs, jet, wine (dossiers/duiblinn.md, dossiers/eoforwic.md). Gilli is invented. Sets ch_york_954_4; _dublin_cargo.

cards.note: Step 5, a turn, optional (scheduled by the lading; drawn at Duiblinn 949 to 953 for anyone past step 2). The town on the Liffey: fenced plots, an earthen bank raised about 950 (Wallace, Wood Quay; dossiers/duiblinn.md), slaves its chief ware. In 951 the foreigners of Dublin plunder Kells and carry off three thousand people, with gold, silver and cattle (Annals of Ulster 951; realms/irish_sea.md) (?). Who held Dublin while Olaf was at York is not certain (?): the card names no lord. The partner and the captive are invented, unnamed. Sets ch_york_954_5 and _dublin_friend; _captives or _ransomed. The road to the Dublin ending runs through this card.

cards.note: Step 6 (drawn at Eoforwic from 952 to the spring of 954). Olaf is driven out, Eric son of Harald is received, and King Eadred has Archbishop Wulfstan shut up at Iudanbyrig. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle E 952 (Ingram 1823: 'This year the Northumbrians expelled King Anlaf, and received Eric the son of Harold') and D 952 (the archbishop 'brought into prison'; Ingram prints the place as Jedburgh, which is not certain (?)). Eric's second coinage, ERIC REX with a sword (Blunt, Stewart and Lyon 1989). That later sagas make him Harald Fairhair's son, called Bloodaxe, is not in any source of his own day (?). Eric's shipmaster Thorgils and the priest are invented. Sets ch_york_954_6; _erics_peace or _wulfstan_letter.

cards.note: Step 8, optional (drawn at Bebbanburg, 952 to midsummer 954, for anyone past step 6). Oswulf, high-reeve of Bamburgh, wants to know when Eric leaves York and by which road. Source: Roger of Wendover, Flores historiarum, under 950: Eric killed on Stainmore 'by the treachery of Earl Oswulf' (proditione Osulfi comitis), by Maccus (our rendering of the Latin); Oswulf earl of all Northumbria afterwards (Historia regum 952 for 954; De primo Saxonum adventu). That he bought news from merchants is invented (?). Cast: Oswulf (real). Sets ch_york_954_8 and _knows_plot; _oswulf_man.

cards.note: Step 10, the choice (drawn at Eoforwic from April to July 954, after step 6). The Northumbrians turn Eric out; he means to go west over Stainmore with his son and his brother. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D and E 954 (Ingram 1823: 'This year the Northumbrians expelled Eric'); Roger of Wendover under 950: killed on Stainmore with his son Haeric and his brother Ragnald, by Maccus son of Olaf, through Oswulf's treachery. The month is not recorded: the game puts the fall after midsummer (?). The four lawmen of York are Domesday's judices, read back (?). That a merchant could offer a hull, send Oswulf word or call the Dublin ships is the game's (history may be changed here). Cast: Thorgils and Ulfketil, invented. Sets ch_york_954_10 and one of _eric_aboard (with the lasting cost ch_york_954_oswulf_feud), _tried, _sent_word, _called_dublin, _stood_town.

cards.note: ENDING: Stainmore, history as it was (drawn at Eoforwic from August 954 to 958 for anyone past step 2 who did not stand with the town, carry Eric or call Dublin; scheduled by step 10). Eric is killed on the moor; King Eadred takes the kingdom; Oswulf is earl; the archbishop is freed but not sent home. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D 954 (Ingram 1823, quoted in the card: 'This year the Northumbrians expelled Eric; and King Edred took to the government of the Northumbrians'); Roger of Wendover under 950 (Maccus, Oswulf, the son and the brother); Wulfstan given Dorchester, not York (ASC D 954). The king's peace given by hand is Domesday's custom at York, read back (?). Flag ch_york_954_end_stainmore. Grand rewards: unlock_charter_eoforwic (with unlock_title_earls_friend and the lasting cost ch_york_954_blood_money for the man who sent word), or unlock_pilot_humber for anyone. Cast: Ulfketil (invented); the king's reeve is invented, unnamed.

cards.note: ENDING: the town's man, history as it was, by the honest road (drawn at Eoforwic from August 954 to 958 for one who stood with the host at step 10; scheduled by it). The kings are gone and the town goes on: the moneyers, the lawmen, the long plots. The hard road pays up to twice the finale and a second grand reward. Sources: as the Stainmore ending; the long fenced plots of the town laid out from about 900 and rebuilt on the same lines (Hall 1984, Coppergate; dossiers/eoforwic.md); Ingelgar struck for Eadred after Eric (Blunt, Stewart and Lyon 1989) (?); sworn witnesses to every sale are King Edgar's law for the Danes a few years on (IV Edgar, about 962) and the game reads the custom back (?). Flag ch_york_954_end_town. Grand rewards: unlock_title_york_sworn_merchant with unlock_plot_eoforwic or unlock_factor_eoforwic; or unlock_plot_eoforwic with unlock_title_archbishops_man. Cast: Ulfketil (invented), Ingelgar (real).

cards.note: ENDING: Eric lives, HISTORY CHANGED (drawn in a Danish or Norse harbour, 954 to 958, for one who carried Eric down the Ouse at step 10). In history he died on Stainmore in 954; here he reached his ships at the Humber mouth and the islands north of Scotland. The later sagas send his widow and sons to Orkney after his death (Heimskringla, Hakonar saga goda c. 4-5; 13th century, not his own day) (?): the game sends him there alive. Flags ch_york_954_end_eric_lives, changed_stainmore_eric_lives; the lasting cost ch_york_954_oswulf_feud was set at step 10. Grand rewards: unlock_ship_norse_allround_ship, or unlock_heirloom_erics_arm_ring, or unlock_title_sea_kings_peace. Cast: Thorgils (invented).

cards.note: ENDING: the Dublin kings hold York, HISTORY CHANGED (drawn at Eoforwic or Duiblinn from August 954 to 958 for one who sent to Dublin at step 10; scheduled by it). In history King Eadred took the kingdom in 954 and no king sat at York again; here Olaf's ships came up the Humber before the English reeves and the lawmen took him a third time. Eric dies on Stainmore in either telling: Wendover's Maccus is 'son of Olaf', and whether that Olaf was of the Dublin house is a guess scholars have made and not proved (?). Olaf Sihtricson himself ruled Dublin to 980 (dossiers/duiblinn.md). Flags ch_york_954_end_dublin, changed_york_dublin_kingdom_954; the lasting cost ch_york_954_eadreds_enemy was set at step 10. Grand rewards: unlock_partner_gilli, or unlock_plot_eoforwic with unlock_charter_eoforwic, or unlock_factor_duiblinn. Cast: Gilli and Ulfketil (invented).
